Index analysis Historical precedent exists: in 2014, hacker Jan Krissler claimed to have reconstructed European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's fingerprint using close-up photos from a press event, and security researchers at Kraken demonstrated constructing a fingerprint from a photo using photo-editing software, a printer and glue. Justin Cappos, a cybersecurity specialist and professor at New York University, characterized the likelihood of fingerprint extraction affecting most individuals as extremely low, stating 'the odds of this happening in your lifetime are slimmer than being hit by a car tomorrow.'
AII-1000-85759: Waymo's fifth-generation autonomous driving system failed to recognize freeway construction zones and drove into them at high speed in at least 13 incidents beginning in early April 2026, with six episodes in Phoenix and seven in the San Francisco Bay Area. The NHTSA recall report stated: 'Under certain circumstances, the AV may enter and drive at speed in freeway construction zones due to inappropriately prioritizing the avoidance of other freeway hazards and/or failing to recognize the construction zone.' The system was installed in Waymo's Jaguar robotaxi fleet, manufactured between May 17, 2022 and May 19, 2026. Reported impact Waymo voluntarily recalled 3,871 robotaxis and restricted freeway operations to address the issue while improvements were developed. One passenger reported the vehicle accelerated between construction work signals and police presence. Index analysis The failure mode involved the autonomous system's inability to detect construction zone signage and lane closures, causing it to prioritize other hazard avoidance over recognizing construction work areas. Governance controls Waymo voluntarily restricted freeway operations, notified state and federal regulators, and filed a voluntary software recall with NHTSA. As of June 13, 2026, the software solution remained in development.
